summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republic reported that Public Administrator Garrard Strode took charge of Allen's tangled estate after executor Simon S. Bass refused to act, and that crowds came to his funeral at Farley & Wand's undertaking rooms.

facts.fact: Public Administrator Garrard Strode took charge of Allen's estate after attorney Simon S. Bass, named executor in the will, refused to act
Allen's funeral took place at 2 p.m. on April 8, 1903, from the Farley & Wand undertaking establishment, 211 South Sixth Street, St. Louis
places: Farley & Wand, 211 South Sixth Street, St. Louis

facts.fact: Pallbearers, mostly former prize fighters, were Chris Lauff, Jack Fletcher, Charley Daly, Tom Kelly, Andy Kirk, Theodore Neusel, Tom O'Donnell and Gus Ellis
At the funeral, Allen's daughter Mrs. Polly Taylor stood with her four children, and Mrs. Tillie Hartgrove also stood by the coffin

notes: Last sentence says Taylor and Hartgrove stood on 'opposite sides of the coffin', then 'on the store [same?] side stood Mrs. Tillie Hartgrove' - likely a typo; 204 says opposite sides. Matches unnumbered fact '000: a public administrator was assigned...'.
